sources.note: Direct original inventory guide read. Weeskamer Batavia 1.04.18.01 and institutional successors. Geometry caveat is independent local decoding, not claimed to derive from this source.

sources.title: Rijksmuseum: Views of VOC establishments at Lawec and Banda, SK-A-4476
sources.note: Direct original object record read: workshop of Johannes Vingboons, circa 1662-1663, provisioning, nutmeg/mace and 1621 violence. Does not adopt compressed assertion that all 15,000 inhabitants were killed or expelled.

sources.title: Rijksmuseum: Jan Brandes, Jantje and Flora in a living room, 1784, NG-1985-7-2-4
sources.note: Original full object page read; description and Opschriften / Merken exact handwritten-text transcription. Drawing dated 1784; sketchbook volume date 1808 is not drawing date. Literal translation supplied editorially; no claim Dutch represents the archipelago’s many Indigenous languages.

sources.title: The Historical Journal: Water Infrastructure as a Technology of Control and a Site of Negotiation in Nineteenth-Century Batavia
sources.note: Original full scholarly article read, section II, footnotes 21 and 28-31. Uses 1873 works, 1876 public opening and Arab community request. Does not backdate 1881 bathing scenes or 1890s health opinions to map period.

sources.title: Leiden University Libraries: Manuscript exhibition for President Widodo, 22 April 2016
sources.note: Original institutional PDF page 1, exhibit 1, BPL 311: botanical manuscript, plant uses, multilingual names and 1741-1750 printing. Later exhibits not used.

sources.title: Norbert Peeters, Leiden Special Collections: Rumphius and his Ambonese Herbal
sources.note: Direct curator/researcher article read: assistance after blindness, copy surviving 1692 ship loss and 1741 first publication. Combined with other herbal source as one conservative work family in focused checks.

sources.title: Rijksmuseum: The Arrest of Diponegoro by Lieutenant General De Kock, SK-A-2238
sources.note: Direct original record read: Java War dates, promised safe conduct and arrest, commission by De Kock, painting circa 1830-1835; painting is retrospective political presentation.

sources.title: Indonesian National Library and KITLV: Babad Diponegoro, UNESCO Memory of the World nomination
sources.note: Original nomination read, PDF pages 1, 3-6: Raffles 1811-1816 and restored administration; exile composition 1831-1832; surviving 1865-1866 Pegon copy KBG282; upbringing with great-grandmother and ulama. Original autograph no longer survives.

sources.title: Nationaal Archief Actorenregister: Afdeling Comptabiliteit, Koloniën
sources.note: Original institutional history read, Geschiedenis, citing F.J.M. Otten 2004 p.358: 1830 cultivation system, compelled crops, fixed prices and colonial fiscal mechanism.

sources.title: Arsip Universitas Indonesia: Gedung FK UI Salemba, Cagar Budaya di Tengah Kota
sources.note: Original university archive account read: January 1851 military-hospital school, twelve first students, Malay-medium subjects; 1849 proposed admission conditions distinguished from actual initial enrollment. Does not use article’s dubious plague chronology.

sources.title: Nationaal Archief: Soevereiniteitsoverdracht Indonesië, 1949
sources.note: Original archival teaching dossier read: declaration 17 August 1945, colonial war and 27 December 1949 transfer. Does not adopt page’s broad 1941 occupation starting date or blanket early territorial-control claim.

proposedOverrides.name: Dutch East Indies
proposedOverrides.summary: Dutch company and colonial government, with changing local relationships, coerced production and a seriously flawed imported map outline.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact indexed record only; no association with later netherlands-indies, dutch-east-indies-1920 or already covered independent indonesia. VOC is an earlier institutional phase, not a new indexed identity.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded six timeline seams in identity.json. Early 1650-1815 archipelago outline bbox about [95.19,-10.38,140.96,5.57] overstates continuous control. The 1815-1878 seam has a Cape/South Africa polygon [17.43,-34.36,25.63,-30.57] and Bangka fragment [105.20,-3.17,106.64,-1.63]. Serious error stated in public overview; geometry has not been repaired.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Imported 1650-1878 maintained as map coverage. Company founded 1602 and nationalized in 1796, charter revoked at start of 1800; Java British interlude 1811-1816; 1830 cultivation system. 1621 Banda explicitly earlier context, and 1945/1949 ending explicitly later. Adjacent period boundaries nonoverlapping.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Dutch Latin-script inscription on Jan Brandes 1784 watercolour NG-1985-7-2-4, exact eight-word fragment plus literal eight-word translation; modern type rather than facsimile. Distinct Javanese Pegon chronicle described without inventing a translated original excerpt.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No universal daily-life or literacy claims. Plantation violence, enslaved household work and imposed crops explained directly without graphic details. Medical history covers training/vaccination, not unverified remedies. Water evidence limited to dated 1873-1876 events, avoiding later bathing anecdotes.
